What is your trick for saving money?
A costo membership, a chest freezer, a rice cooker/veggie steamer and a grill press. I can make three healthy chicken dinners in a half hour for less than around 2 bucks a meal.
I forgot the PIN for my savings account, so I don't touch it. If I want access to the money, I have to go to the bank. It makes frivolous spending easier to avoid.

It is so easy to spend a few bucks here and a few there especially when you see sales. The thinking, "Oh, its on sale, so I'm saving money if I get it now." is a lie. The only way to save money is to not spend it. Also, candy bars, drinks, songs, apps, etc. even though are only a dollar or two add up quickly!

No matter how much you make, always take at least 10% and put it in a retirement savings account (either 401k or an IRA). The retirement savings is money you will not touch until you retire. Have this done automatically if you can so you never even see the money in your paycheck. Start as soon as you can since the investment will compound over time. A little pinch now is a lot better then a big bite later.

Then create a budget with all your remaining expenses and income mapped out. There should be a surplus between your fixed expenses and income. If no surplus, then you need more money- easier said then done I know. You then take the surplus and put some or all of it into a savings account each month. Most banks will allow you to do an automatic transfer from checking into savings.

Having a savings goal can also really help. New phone, new car, down payment for a house- whatever. Remember that is can be okay to withdraw from savings if you meet your savings goal.

Look around for the best rate in a savings account- you should be getting at least a .75% interest rate from your savings account.

As you build up savings as cash you will run into a point where you have 'too much' cash in the bank. Due to inflation, cash in the bank is actually worth less and less each year. Of course you want some cash on hand in case of emergency but you will also want to start looking at investments that will preform better then inflation. With investment there is risk of loss, but there are some funds that in the long run will outperform inflation and if they don't you better be thinking more about how to grow food since shit has hit the fan (SPY is a good index fund that is pretty safe for long term investment).

Find hobbies that are free. It costs nothing to take a walk in the park or to learn some new skills online like how to fix your own car. Quit expensive habits like tabacco/alcohol.

Eat out less and drink less. A single meal with alcohol and tip can cost as much as a weeks worth of groceries at the store. Also pack lunches for work you'll save ~$15 a day not diving and buying lunch.

Another would be to only use your credit card when needed. Dont spend money you dont have and never anticipate money coming in that is not guaranteed. Create a budget and know how much you bring in each month and make sure you spend less that that.

Buy used items when possible to save some money or when buying new things always price compare and use coupons.
